So too, when punishments are given you, you must accept them with humility even though you do not deserve them; instead there have been some who complained and said so many things: Oh! I am fed up! In a moment I shall not know what to do! Oh! yes, the Lord will know well how to punish such a one, since, as much as He rewards good and humble actions, so much will He punish proud ones. So too, if you knew how much harm that sister did at the sick woman’s house! There, now you can touch with your hand whether I am right to preach cleanliness. I recommend to you: be careful when you blow your nose, blow it with good manners; do not wipe your mouth with your hands; do not wipe away sweat with moderation [?]; sneeze softly; sit composedly, with modesty; even if one is not well brought up, modesty alone teaches it to you.

The daughter of Saint Anne must be, as our Holy Father Pius IX said, “an apostle who preaches the faith with her good actions and good example: to those who are religious, to increase them ever more in their fervour; to those who are religious [?], to draw them to devotion, or at least to make them Christians”. On the street, at the bedside of the sick, she must preach modesty with her bearing, with her eyes, with her words; instead you do the reverse, and in this way you wound the Heart of the Lord God. Nothing remains for me to say but: raise your right hand and strike; free [?] our Institute from whoever does not wish to nourish the true spirit of our Rules, which is yours [?]; may the Lord deliver us.

given at Piacenza on 25 July 1872

On charity

It seems impossible to me that, after the fourth time that I hold Chapter, I must always set my hand to reproofs and punishments. When will it be that you, this House of Piacenza, set yourselves on the way of perfection, that you put into practice your Holy Rules, Charity, bearing with one another? It truly seems that in this house these virtues have taken flight and that the devil dwells in it instead. And do you perhaps believe that it is a small sorrow for me, that it does not tear my soul, to have always to preach to you and never obtain anything? Yes, this makes me think that it is I who give you scandal and that all the harm comes from me.

Let us begin to speak about charity towards the sick: this is badly exercised. If the one who acts as first fails, the one who acts as second, perhaps humiliated because the superior has given her that place, in her pride, her self-love, notices the failing the sister commits, but she keeps silent, she does not speak, even if she sees her poisoning the sick person, and says: but the Superior has put her first, and I have let her do as she pleases; I noticed that the sick person was not content, but it does not matter to me at all, it is for her to see to it. And in this way she lets the sick person be torn to pieces under the claws of the other. Oh! wickedness without end! And what are you going to the sick for? It would be better for you to go off to Purgatory than to act so; and where is your charity? But it is honour that drives me to keep silent. Charity has no honour; rather, to hear this said to me by a daughter of Saint Anne, who ought not even to know what honour is, truly makes me shudder. Perhaps the Superior, to test your humility and for some purpose of her own, which I do not go about investigating, makes you act as second while you are first by vocation; and you, for this, heeding your ugly self-love, say within yourself: Oh! the Superior has done this, I shall let the sick person die. Ah! yes, up to now it is only in this house that this is seen, and that I have such sorrows, and things that have happened in these days. And is this how you waste so holy a mission which God has given you? Think about it a little seriously. To you infirmarians I give this as your examen for the month, because here there is no charity, and where there is no charity one cannot have a tranquil conscience.

Confess it; and until you give your self-love into the hands of the Superiors and go to the house of the sick with a true spirit of everything [?], you will tell me whether what I tell you is true. When you are with the sick, pay no heed to first or second; see to doing your office well, both of you; the Lord may give more light to one than to the other, more to the second than to the first. You must help one another, intent on relieving the sick person. Whether first or second, you are all equal. For example: it comes to the mind of one to do something, to arrange the sick person in one way rather than another, thinking that perhaps he will be better so; one says: Sister, let us do this, let us relieve him in this way, with this thing. So then, have you understood? Relieve the sick person both of you, in holy harmony.

You are two at work; one says one thing, the other says another, all for the benefit of the poor sick person; well then, let us try both things: that is charity. Do you know why a first and a second are appointed? Because if there should be need to speak, to give some account to the Doctor, the one who is first by vocation, having more knowledge, can give them better and more exactly; that is why a first and a second are appointed, and for no other reason. I hope you have all understood and will make a promise to the Holy Mother never again to commit this fault; and if anyone should feel it always sprouting within her, let her pray to her that it may never return. There is another point in which you fail, and it is obedience; and it is for this that God gives you grace and then takes it away from you. The Superior gives the obedience to go to the sick and tells you to be quick; instead you tire yourselves looking for the veil, the apron, and you go after an hour. She will tell you also to do something, and there at once, before doing it, you make a thousand observations. If we knew this word, Obedience, we should not make so many reflections on what is commanded us. So too, the one who complains about the food must go to the Superior, not to the cook, as some do. Indeed I cannot understand how one who has given herself to God should think of the swine of her body, of keeping it well fed. I do not say this of all, because, I repeat, there are good ones. Indeed, you see, the cause of your ill is I alone, for having indulged your wishes too much; but what I have not known how to do, the Holy Mother has known how to do: to put a bridle on you. She, who is that holy Matron who conceived the divine Mary and who consequently was filled with virtue, cannot bear to see her daughters so lacking in it. Believe me, at first she will know how to bear with the guilty, but then she will know well how to rid herself of them. Believe me that what I do not know how to do, she knows how to do, she who is so powerful; where the creature does not reach, God reaches. How I should have wished that now, since some sisters have to return from a house, from a House, they had found order. Indeed, this there is. But you must be kept with the whip, with so many eyes, now so that you may be in chapel, now at dinner, etc., instead of chattering, gossiping about the Superior, about one House, about another. You see, in the other houses there is not this spirit. So then, if you wish to begin to do a little good, begin now that we are in the month of the Holy Mother. Set yourselves to begin a new life, to be all eyes for your salvation; let your conversations always be of God, because if you suffer [?] from this, you go on to murmuring, for what do you expect your conversations to be? Or else, out of a spirit of charity, after having relieved one sister, pass on to another. You have a free moment: try to go off to Church; so too during the day make some spiritual communions, which you will find again at the pillow of your death, and they will make your death sweet for you. I know well that the Religious life, for one who comes out of the world, proves a painful life, all the more because she does not know the love of God. Do you no longer remember for what reason you came into Religion? To become saints, and little by little to ascend to the love of God. Indeed, to speak of this to you is to speak Arabic, but even so you must reach this divine love. I must also tell you not to be dismayed if the feast of Saint Anne is not kept this year; it is not for nothing; our Institute is running under full sail. There will be only two Masses and the exposition of her relic, for in this way I believe I honour the Holy Mother

Sayings of the Mother on various faults

4 August 1872

Tell me: you know that from the sick nothing may be taken; and yet there are many who have made it lawful for themselves to take ice; and does this seem to you to be observing the Rules? It matters little that they say Paters and Aves and then fail in the most important things, which are our Holy Rules.

It seems impossible that a daughter of Saint Anne should be so little mortified as not to be able to drink water a little warmer; it means that your palate draws you to the greatest gluttony, and you do not know how to make a small mortification. All these days I have been observing you, and I see that you give yourselves no reason to become more mortified, further on in the religious life.

I have told you so many times how much God accepts these small mortifications, especially of the palate. Truly it must be I who give you bad example, and I am becoming ever more persuaded of it; but you read so many books about new foundations, and you have heard what these holy founders did, how mortified and penitent they were; and then how many times have you heard it preached, both in words and by example, by the Father! Oh! listen: it is because there is no obedience, and where this is lacking there can be no mortification.

Truly, the other day I felt as though boiling water had been thrown on my brain when I was told by the refectorian that many had left their coffee because it was not sweet enough. Oh! you have become very delicate; and do you no longer remember what was told you at the porter’s lodge when you presented yourselves to be admitted? That here you must take up a life of hardship, of mortifications. And then you cannot take coffee that is perhaps a little less sweet?

It is more than 40 years and more that my lips have not tasted coffee with sugar; and if I take coffee, my Superiors know it, God knows it; and nevertheless I do not fail to draw from this coffee some gain of perfection.

Truly I tell you that for some days now you have taken from me even my words, and you take away my life by always giving me new displeasures, as I must always reprove you for modesty — which, as I have told you several times, is never too much — whether of the hands, of the eyes, or of the bearing. Oh! yes, you make me die of anguish at every moment, to think that a work as great as ours, a work of charity, you trample upon it; and I feel my blood run cold when reading of the virtues of the first followers of founders, who were so mortified, so penitent. You have no excuse: your foundress is Saint Anne. She united all the virtues in a heroic degree; and so I am the donkey who leads myself to Her; but you must not look at me, but rather at Her, who is your Mother.

We have Rules that have nothing but an unction of holiness, and those who have read them have said several times that she who observed them would certainly become a Saint; but in my heart, while they were being explained to you, ah! how far it will be from their being observed! [?] And then we want God to grant us graces. I see in you a certain laxity, so that you go to church and say all your prayers pushed along by the current. In short, it is now time that you put an end to it; I hoped for it in the novena of the Holy Mother, and God knows how many prayers I have said for you. Begin now a better life; the Holy Mother is weary of your laxities. I repeat to you: with the sick we must not raise our eyes to anyone’s face, nor pin up our scapular with pins in front of one another, because if we are in front of men we shall give occasion for them to form bad thoughts, and if they are women they will laugh at us. When we are with the sick we must cover them, do only what modesty permits, and as I have taught you; you must practise this virtue so dear to God, and all of you practise it; and not that today a more scrupulous one goes and does as I have taught, uses modesty in touching them, with the eyes, etc., and tomorrow another goes, less reserved, with a broader conscience, who pays no heed, pulls the sick person about without reserve, so that she gives occasion for the sick person to say: this sister does it one way, that one another. The daughters of Saint Anne must all be alike, so that the sick may not say: send me this one, send me that other one.

You will say to me: but I see Jesus in the sick person. You must look to obedience and conduct yourselves as obedience teaches you, to be one in all; for I no longer wish to hear it said: one does me more good than the other. And so as not to hear this said any more, every Sunday there will be the school for infirmarians; and if there should be one who heard a sick person say that she had done a procedure better than another, the Superior, once that one has returned home, will have them all gathered and will do the same thing to that Sister who did not do it well, and will do so until she has learnt it well; and so too she will do with all the others, so that all may serve the sick equally well, since we must all have the same way of serving, caring for and comforting the sick.
